title: A Crow
html:
• Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.77 Numbered Discourses 10.77
  • 8. Ākaṅkhavagga 8. If You Want

Kākasutta A Crow

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, asaddhammehi samannāgato kāko. “Mendicants, a crow possesses ten bad qualities. Katamehi dasahi? What ten? Dhaṁsī ca, pagabbho ca, tintiṇo ca, mahagghaso ca, luddo ca, akāruṇiko ca, dubbalo ca, oravitā ca, muṭṭhassati ca, necayiko ca—They’re rude and impudent, gluttonous and voracious, cruel and pitiless, weak and raucous, unmindful and acquisitive. imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato kāko. A crow possesses these ten bad qualities. Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhu. In the same way, a bad mendicant possesses these ten bad qualities. Katamehi dasahi? What ten? Dhaṁsī ca, pagabbho ca, tintiṇo ca, mahagghaso ca, luddo ca, akāruṇiko ca, dubbalo ca, oravitā ca, muṭṭhassati ca, necayiko ca—They’re rude and impudent, gluttonous and voracious, cruel and pitiless, weak and raucous, unmindful and acquisitive. imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhū”ti. A bad mendicant possesses these ten bad qualities.”

Sattamaṁ.
